messages:
paging-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — routing-oscillation detected for service/redwood-api (text-generation). p95 > 500ms in us-west, multiple automatic reroutes observed. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/routing/alerts/1750004321 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Severity: P2. Trigger: latency-slo-flap. Notifying on-call (ryan) and eng-runtime.
ryan: on it. looking at traces now. any early context?
ana: pinging in — I see repeated 'route_change' events every ~30s between us-west (v2-quant) and us-east (v1). looks like the routing policy keeps swapping back and forth.
ryan: hmm. is it the model variant mismatch? we had mention of auto-fallback to v1 for capacity, but v1 has different tokenization/kv cache behavior.
mike: infra metrics show cold kv-cache misses spike right after a switch. that pushes p95 up, which then flips routing back. loop.
lee: network looks fine, no packet loss. egress bw stable.
sanjay: logs (excerpt):
```
policy-evaluator: eval_id=abc123 reason=p95_exceeded target=us-east-v1 previous=us-west-v2 rule=latency_slo_95
runtime: start_attach_model us-east-v1 request_id=xyz
runtime: kv_cache_miss=1.0 attach_time_ms=420
policy-evaluator: eval_id=abc124 reason=p95_exceeded target=us-west-v2 previous=us-east-v1 rule=latency_slo_95
```
ryan: ok that's the fingerprint. attaching v1 causes cold start hits -> p95 goes up -> policy flips -> back and forth. we also have a policy configured to prefer lower-cost variant automatically when p95 > 250ms — suspect misconfigured thresholds.
jen-cs: any customer-facing impact? Acme reported degraded performance ~5m ago.
sanjay: current affected orgs: 12 orgs, 3 with high error/latency alerts (Acme, NovaPay, Tradify). no increased error rate, mostly latency.
emma-product: we should prioritize stable routing for paid tenants. can we pin them?
ana: recommended mitigation: 1) pause smart-routing policy for the route, 2) pin to the higher-stability variant (us-west-v2) for now, 3) increase routing hysteresis (p95 window to 5m) to avoid oscillation.
ryan: agree. can someone run the pause and pin commands? I don't have admin for policy changes.
mike: doing CLI: `redwoodctl policies pause --id latency_slo_95 --env hosted` -> submitted.
anna (typo??) : (system message) policy latency_slo_95 paused by mike at 1750004442
ryan: mike — confirm pinning to us-west-v2 for affected accounts?
mike: `redwoodctl routes pin --route /v1/generate --variant us-west-v2 --org acme,nova,tradify` -> applied at 1750004460
lee: monitoring shows p95 dropping after pin. current p95 (us-west-v2) = 220ms, previous oscillation spikes ~600ms.
sanjay: still seeing a couple of flips in logs; might be older events draining. give it ~2min.
jen-cs: I posted proactive note to impacted customers: "We're aware of elevated latency; we've applied a mitigation and are monitoring. Will update with follow-up."
emma-product: thanks. please capture exact timelines for postmortem.
ryan: assigning on-call handoff: I need to go offline in ~20m. ana, can you take the rest of the incident?
ana: taking over. I'll keep monitoring, coordinate with runtime. next steps: 1) confirm full stabilization, 2) rollback any recent policy changes that cause auto-fallback to cheaper variant, 3) run canary for config change in staging, 4) follow-up postmortem.
ryan: leaving notes in incident doc: https://wiki.redwood.local/incidents/1750004321
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial. Mitigation applied: smart-routing paused; pin applied to us-west-v2 for affected orgs.
sanjay: quick root-cause theory: latency-based routing policy uses short sample window (30s) and has lower-cost bias that favors v1 on capacity triggers. Combined with cold-kv behavior for v1 caused p95 spikes immediately after switch. No circuit-breaker/hysteresis to prevent oscillation.
lee: suggested durable fixes: - add hysteresis (5-10m) on p95 based routing - require warmup (pre-warm KV cache) before switching model variants - decouple model-variant switches from region failover for first 10m - add flip-rate limiter in policy evaluator
ana: I've scheduled a follow-up action item: ENG-RUNTIME to own policy change; due by EOD. Product and CS to coordinate customer comms.
jen-cs: will follow up with impacted customers with ETA.
ryan: thanks team. leaving in ana's hands. I'm out. :wave:
ana: will update here with stabilization timestamp. current status: p95 steady ~210-240ms for last 4m. marking incident as "mitigated (policy paused + pins)".
emma-product: please include cost/regression tradeoffs in postmortem proposals.
incident-bot: Incident closed for paging; follow-up tasks created: low, root-cause-investigation, postmortem required.
